sections.sectionTitle: Section A: Language (Usem / Tsarin Sauti da Nahawu)

topics.title: Comprehension, Essay Writing, Sound System, Grammar, and Translation

subtopics.content: Reading passages, essay/letter writing, Ibibio phonetics/phonology, syllable structure, tone marks, word formation, word classes, grammatical categories, phrases/clauses, sentence structures, and translation
subtopics.objective: Comprehend written Ibibio texts; write 300-word compositions (narrative, descriptive, letter writing) using standard orthography; describe Ibibio vowels, consonants, syllabic nasals, assimilation, and tones (high, low, falling, rising); analyze word roots, affixes, word classes, tenses, negation, phrases, clauses, and sentence types; translate accurately between English and Ibibio.

topics.title: Literary Appreciation, Oral Literature, and Written Literature

subtopics.content: Literary appreciation principles, prescribed oral literature (folktales, songs, traditional drama), and prescribed written literature (prose, poetry, drama)
subtopics.objective: Apply basic principles of literary appreciation; analyze prescribed oral literature texts (*Mbak Anyan-idaha*, *Kap Toiyo: Mme Uto Ibibio*, *Mbre ke Ibibio: Ma Ñkpo Mfo*); critique prescribed written prose (*Ufokñwed Idañ*); evaluate set written poetry (*Mben Idim Anie Adion*); study prescribed written drama (*Uwa*).

sections.sectionTitle: Section C: Culture (Edu Uwem da Mme Usọrọ)

topics.title: Customs, Institutions, Rites, and Ibibio Worldview

subtopics.content: Traditional occupations, family structure, religious institutions, traditional foods, funeral rites, traditional festivals, taboos (Ibed), traditional education, coronation, maiden fattening (Mboppo), and traditional societies
subtopics.objective: Identify traditional Ibibio occupations (fishing, farming, weaving, carving); understand family structures and religious systems; describe traditional foods and funeral practices; detail festivals (Usọrọ Idọk, Usio Mboppo) and cultural taboos; evaluate traditional education, coronation rites, Mboppo maiden fattening, secret societies, and the Ibibio worldview.
